title: Boolean logic
examples: What is the difference between an AND gate and an OR gate?
Can you show me how to simplify a complex logic expression?
When do we use XOR gates in real electronics?

explain.say: Today we are learning about Boolean logic gates. These gates help computers make decisions.

draw.text: Boolean Logic Gates: AND, OR, NOT

explain.say: The AND gate only gives a true output when all its inputs are true. Think of it like needing two keys.

draw.text: AND: A AND B = True only if A and B are True

explain.say: The OR gate gives a true output if at least one of its inputs is true. It only needs one key to work.

draw.text: OR: A OR B = True if A or B is True

explain.say: The NOT gate simply reverses a single input. If the input is true, the output becomes false.

draw.text: NOT: NOT A = Opposite of A

explain.say: The XOR gate gives true only when its inputs are different. One must be true, and the other must be false.

draw.text: XOR: A XOR B = True if A is not equal to B

explain.say: In real life, think about a security alarm system. It might need an AND gate to trigger. Both the door sensor and the window sensor must trip.

draw.text: Real Life: Alarm needs Door AND Window open

faq.q: What is the difference between AND and OR gates?
faq.a: The AND gate requires all inputs to be true for the output to be true. The OR gate only needs one input to be true for the output to be true.
asks: When is an AND gate true?
How is OR different from AND?

faq.a: Simplification means making a complex logical statement shorter without changing its meaning. You are finding the simplest equivalent form.
asks: How do I make logic simpler?

faq.q: Do I need to know all the gates to pass the test?
faq.a: Understanding the basic function of AND, OR, NOT, and XOR is most important. They are the building blocks for everything else.
asks: Are there other gates I should know?

faq.a: A truth table shows all possible combinations of inputs and the resulting output for a logic gate. It helps us predict the gate's behavior.
asks: How do I read a truth table?

faq.q: Is Boolean logic only for computers?
faq.a: No, Boolean logic is a mathematical system used to represent true or false statements. It is used in many areas beyond just computers.
asks: Is this math used anywhere else?
Is it just for digital circuits?

facts: Boolean logic deals only with two values: true or false.
The AND gate output is only true when every input is true.
The NOT gate inverts the logic state of its single input.
XOR is true only when inputs are different (one true, one false).

quiz.say: If Input A is true and Input B is false, what is the output of an AND gate?
quiz.why: The AND gate requires both inputs to be true to output true, so one false input makes it false.

wrong.1: This is wrong because the AND gate is very strict and needs everything to be true.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the gate will always give a definite true or false answer.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the output depends on the specific combination of true and false inputs.

quiz.say: What is the output of an OR gate if Input A is false and Input B is true?
quiz.why: The OR gate only needs one input to be true, and in this case, Input B is true.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the presence of a true input guarantees a true output.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the OR gate has a clear rule for when it outputs true.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the OR gate is satisfied by just one true input.

quiz.say: If we have the expression (A OR B) AND NOT A, what is the simplest output?
quiz.why: If you expand the expression, the terms involving A cancel out, leaving only B as the necessary condition for the whole statement to be true.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the NOT A part removes the dependency on A in the final result.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the expression can be true if B is true and A is false.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the NOT A part restricts the possibilities too much.
